answer: The anchor multiplier is published, charged in ember, and lantern lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4617 identities would post 2875 proofs and burn roughly 5 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
